name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
      - uses: actions/setup-go@v6
        with:
          go-version: "1.26.x"
          cache: false
      - run: go test ./...
      - run: go vet ./...

  docker:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
      - uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v4
      - uses: docker/build-push-action@v7
        with:
          context: .
          push: false
          tags: minio-compat:test

name: Container image

on:
  push:
    tags: ["v*"]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  packages: write

jobs:
  publish:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
      - uses: docker/setup-qemu-action@v4
      - uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v4
      - uses: docker/login-action@v4
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      - id: meta
        uses: docker/metadata-action@v6
        with:
          images: ghcr.io/seaweedfs/minio-compat
          tags: |
            type=semver,pattern={{version}}
            type=semver,pattern={{major}}.{{minor}}
            type=raw,value=latest
      - uses: docker/build-push-action@v7
        with:
          context: .
          platforms: linux/amd64,linux/arm64
          push: true
          tags: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.tags }}
          labels: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.labels }}
          build-args: VERSION=${{ github.ref_name }}

# SeaweedFS MinIO compatibility image

`minio-compat` is a thin container image that lets common single-node MinIO
Docker deployments start SeaweedFS with a very small configuration change. It
keeps the familiar `minio server` command, `MINIO_*` environment variables,
ports 9000/9001, and MinIO health-check URLs.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> This is a command-line and deployment compatibility layer, not an on-disk
> format converter. Never attach an existing MinIO data volume to this image.
> Migrate objects through the S3 API into a new volume.

## Quick start

Typical MinIO command:

```sh
docker run --name minio \
  -p 9000:9000 -p 9001:9001 \
  -e MINIO_ROOT_USER=admin \
  -e MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD=[REDACTED] \
  -v minio-data:/data \
  quay.io/minio/minio server /data --console-address :9001
```

SeaweedFS replacement (new empty volume required):

```sh
docker run --name minio \
  -p 9000:9000 -p 9001:9001 \
  -e MINIO_ROOT_USER=admin \
  -e MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD=[REDACTED] \
  -v seaweedfs-data:/data \
  ghcr.io/seaweedfs/minio-compat:latest server /data --console-address :9001
```

The S3 endpoint remains `http://localhost:9000`. Port 9001 serves the
SeaweedFS Admin UI rather than the MinIO Console. The same root credentials
protect both interfaces.

### Docker Compose

For a common single-node Compose service, change the image and allocate a new
volume; the command, environment, ports, and health check can stay unchanged:

```yaml
services:
  minio:
    image: ghcr.io/seaweedfs/minio-compat:latest
    command: server /data --console-address :9001
    environment:
      MINIO_ROOT_USER: admin
      MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD: [REDACTED]
    ports:
      - "9000:9000"
      - "9001:9001"
    volumes:
      - seaweedfs-data:/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "curl", "-f", "http://localhost:9000/minio/health/live"]

volumes:
  seaweedfs-data:
```

## Migrate data safely

Run old MinIO and this image at the same time, backed by different volumes and
reachable on different host ports. Then copy through S3:

```sh
mc alias set old http://localhost:9000 OLD_ACCESS_KEY OLD_SECRET_KEY
mc alias set new http://localhost:19000 NEW_ACCESS_KEY NEW_SECRET_KEY
mc mirror --overwrite old new
```

Verify object counts, sizes, metadata, application reads, and bucket policies
before switching clients. `mc mirror` does not turn a MinIO filesystem into a
SeaweedFS filesystem and should not be pointed at either product's data
directory. Plan version-history and IAM migration separately when those
features are in use.

## Compatibility

Supported:

- `minio server DIR`
- `--address` and `--console-address`, including `--flag=value`
- `MINIO_ROOT_USER` / `MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD`
- legacy `MINIO_ACCESS_KEY` / `MINIO_SECRET_KEY`
- matching Docker secret `_FILE` variables
- `MINIO_ADDRESS`, `MINIO_CONSOLE_ADDRESS`, `MINIO_BROWSER`
- `MINIO_DOMAIN` and `MINIO_SERVER_URL`
- `MINIO_VOLUMES`, `MINIO_ARGS`, and `MINIO_ENDPOINTS` for local directories
- `/minio/health/live`, `/ready`, `/cluster`, and `/cluster/read`
- normal S3 clients, including `mc`, AWS SDKs, and AWS CLI

Deliberately not supported:

- reusing MinIO's `.minio.sys` or other MinIO on-disk data
- multiple local data directories in this single-node transition image
- distributed MinIO endpoint URLs and `{1...4}` ellipsis expansion
- MinIO TLS flags; terminate TLS at a reverse proxy and set
  `MINIO_SERVER_URL=https://your-s3-host`
- MinIO Console behavior or `mc admin` management APIs
- every MinIO-specific extension; test workloads before production cutover

The adapter uses SeaweedFS's MinIO-compatible S3 behavior: buckets are not
created implicitly and non-empty buckets cannot be deleted in one operation.

## Build and test

```sh
make test
docker build -t minio-compat:dev .
```

The image is intentionally small in scope: a static adapter binary is layered
on the official `chrislusf/seaweedfs` image. SeaweedFS remains the storage
server and receives normal SeaweedFS configuration variables.

## Security

Set explicit production credentials. The MinIO-compatible defaults
(`minioadmin` / `minioadmin`) exist only to match local MinIO behavior. Root
secrets are passed to SeaweedFS through environment variables and are not
written into process arguments or the generated `mini.options` file.

Report security issues according to the
[SeaweedFS security policy](https://github.com/seaweedfs/seaweedfs/security/policy).

# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1

ARG SEAWEEDFS_IMAGE=chrislusf/seaweedfs:latest

FROM --platform=$BUILDPLATFORM golang:1.26-alpine AS builder
WORKDIR /src
COPY go.mod ./
COPY cmd ./cmd
COPY internal ./internal
ARG TARGETOS
ARG TARGETARCH
ARG VERSION=dev
RUN CGO_ENABLED=0 GOOS=$TARGETOS GOARCH=$TARGETARCH \
    go build -trimpath -ldflags "-s -w -X main.Version=$VERSION" \
    -o /out/minio-compat ./cmd/minio-compat

FROM ${SEAWEEDFS_IMAGE}
USER root
COPY --from=builder /out/minio-compat /usr/local/bin/minio-compat
COPY --chmod=0755 entrypoint.sh /usr/local/bin/minio-entrypoint

LABEL org.opencontainers.image.title="SeaweedFS MinIO compatibility image" \
      org.opencontainers.image.description="A thin SeaweedFS image compatible with common MinIO Docker commands" \
      org.opencontainers.image.source="https://github.com/seaweedfs/minio-compat" \
      org.opencontainers.image.licenses="Apache-2.0"

EXPOSE 9000 9001
ENTRYPOINT ["/usr/local/bin/minio-entrypoint"]
CMD ["server", "/data", "--console-address", ":9001"]

.PHONY: build test docker-build

build:
	go build ./cmd/minio-compat

test:
	go test ./...
	go vet ./...

docker-build:
	docker build -t minio-compat:dev .

#!/bin/sh
set -eu

# Match the upstream SeaweedFS image default while allowing operators to opt
# out with GODEBUG=fips140=off.
export GODEBUG="${GODEBUG:+$GODEBUG,}fips140=on"

data_dir=""
seen_server=false
skip_next=false
for arg in "$@"; do
  if [ "$skip_next" = true ]; then
    skip_next=false
    continue
  fi
  if [ "$seen_server" = false ]; then
    if [ "$arg" = "server" ]; then
      seen_server=true
    fi
    continue
  fi
  case "$arg" in
    --address|--console-address)
      skip_next=true
      ;;
    --*)
      ;;
    *)
      data_dir="$arg"
      break
      ;;
  esac
done

if [ -z "$data_dir" ]; then
  for value in "${MINIO_ARGS:-}" "${MINIO_VOLUMES:-}" "${MINIO_ENDPOINTS:-}"; do
    if [ -n "$value" ]; then
      # The adapter accepts exactly one local path, so whitespace splitting is
      # equivalent to the Go parser for these compatibility variables.
      set -- $value
      data_dir="$1"
      break
    fi
  done
fi
if [ -z "$data_dir" ]; then
  data_dir="/data"
fi

if [ -e "$data_dir/.minio.sys" ]; then
  echo "minio compatibility error: $data_dir contains MinIO on-disk data, which SeaweedFS cannot open in place" >&2
  echo "Copy objects through S3 into a new volume; see the migration guide in the repository README." >&2
  exit 2
fi

if [ "$(id -u)" = "0" ]; then
	case "$data_dir" in
		*://*|*\{*|*\}*)
			# Let the adapter produce the detailed unsupported-layout error.
			data_dir="/data"
			;;
	esac
	mkdir -p "$data_dir"
  seaweed_uid="$(id -u seaweed)"
  seaweed_gid="$(id -g seaweed)"
  data_uid="$(stat -c '%u' "$data_dir" 2>/dev/null || true)"
  data_gid="$(stat -c '%g' "$data_dir" 2>/dev/null || true)"

  if [ "$data_uid" != "$seaweed_uid" ] || [ "$data_gid" != "$seaweed_gid" ]; then
    echo "Fixing $data_dir ownership for seaweed user (uid=$seaweed_uid, gid=$seaweed_gid)"
    if ! chown -R seaweed:seaweed "$data_dir"; then
      echo "warning: could not change $data_dir ownership; startup may fail if it is not writable" >&2
    fi
  fi

  exec su-exec seaweed "$0" "$@"
fi

exec /usr/local/bin/minio-compat "$@"
